findings.statement: Baseline NFkB pathway activity is higher in ustekinumab non-responders (BH padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000484]), but it is equally associated with non-response in the UNIFI placebo arm (BH padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.00608]), so this marks severity rather than a drug-specific mechanism. TNFa behaves the same way, significant in all four drug arms and UNIFI placebo.

In the PURSUIT placebo arm the NFkB association with non-response is absent (BH padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (PURSUIT).padj=0.932]); that arm is small, so the lack of signal is weak evidence.

JAK-STAT activity is higher in ustekinumab non-responders (BH padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0124]) but does not reach significance for golimumab (BH padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.golimumab.padj=0.204]); it is also nominally higher in UNIFI placebo non-responders, so severity contributes.

TGFb pathway activity is associated with ustekinumab non-response (BH padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.000493]) but not golimumab non-response (BH padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.golimumab.padj=0.348]); UNIFI placebo is also significant, so it is not clearly drug-specific.

Baseline OSM is higher in ustekinumab non-responders (BH padj [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000264]), but the drug-vs-placebo interaction is null (padj [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; interaction.ustekinumab.padj=0.971]) and UNIFI placebo is similar in direction (padj [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.116]). Nothing survives correction in golimumab, infliximab or vedolizumab, so OSM looks like a severity marker rather than a ustekinumab-specific one.

TREM1 is higher in ustekinumab non-responders (BH padj [gene=TREM1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000474]) and also in UNIFI placebo non-responders (BH padj [gene=TREM1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0234]), consistent with severity; the other biologic arms do not survive correction.

IL11 shows the strongest ustekinumab association among the genes tested (BH padj [gene=IL11; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=3.68e-8]), but it also separates UNIFI placebo non-responders (BH padj [gene=IL11; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0133]), and the interaction test is not significant, so it marks severity.

CXCR2 is the top convergence candidate (meta-analysis log2FC [gene=CXCR2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=2.264], up in five cohorts, with clinical-stage antagonists). Its baseline level is associated with ustekinumab non-response (BH padj [gene=CXCR2; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=9.69e-6]) but equally with UNIFI placebo non-response (BH padj [gene=CXCR2; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0126]), so the response signal is severity-linked and likely neutrophil-driven.

CXCL8 is higher in ustekinumab non-responders (BH padj [gene=CXCL8; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.000102]) and in UNIFI placebo non-responders (BH padj [gene=CXCL8; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0154]); no golimumab, infliximab or vedolizumab difference survives correction.

Baseline IL23A, the ustekinumab target pathway, is not associated with ustekinumab response (BH padj [gene=IL23A; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.977]); target expression does not mark response.
Baseline ITGB7, the vedolizumab target subunit, is not associated with vedolizumab response (BH padj [gene=ITGB7; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.vedolizumab.padj=0.995]).

LAX1 is the top first-in-class candidate (up in five cohorts, antibody-tractable) but is flagged partly composition-driven, with only a fraction retained after composition adjustment (retained [gene=LAX1; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; retained=0.23]). Single-cell data place it mainly in plasma cells and T cells, so the signal largely reflects infiltrating immune cells and the second dataset does not replicate the T/NK lineage.

XKR9 is epithelial-intrinsic but replicated in only a small number of cohorts (cohorts up [gene=XKR9; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; cohorts_up=2]), few cells express it, and the second dataset points to plasma cells, so support is thin.

SDR16C5 is the cleanest epithelial candidate, with most of its signal retained after composition adjustment (retained [gene=SDR16C5; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; retained=0.66]) and the epithelial lineage confirmed in the second dataset. Missing are functional or genetic support and any response-cohort data.

CHRDL2 is stromal, mainly inflammatory fibroblasts, with the lineage replicated in the second dataset, but it has appreciable RNA in a vital organ (max HPA nTPM [gene=CHRDL2; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; vital_max_ntpm=42.6]) and is partly composition-driven, which is a safety flag to resolve.

ADGRG3 is classed as a first-in-class opportunity, but its transcripts are almost entirely neutrophil-derived (neutrophil share [gene=ADGRG3; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; neutrophil_share=0.906]), so it is a neutrophil-abundance readout rather than a tissue-intrinsic change.

caveats: Response cohorts are small except UNIFI ustekinumab; infliximab and vedolizumab arms have few responders, so the lack of significance there is not evidence of absence.
Many ustekinumab associations match the UNIFI placebo arm and the drug-vs-placebo interaction is null for the genes tested, so they reflect severity, not drug-specific mechanism.
Associations are baseline, bulk-tissue and cross-sectional; they are not predictions and need prospective validation.
The discovery screen is bulk plus single-cell derived and has no functional or genetic validation; neutrophils are absent from the Smillie dataset.
Only the first few discovery candidates were profiled.
